:::{#def-quadratic-model}
#### Quadratic model (second-order Taylor polynomial)

Let $f$ be as in @def-newton-method and let $\vx$ be a point,
with $\vecf{g} \eqdef \deriv{\vx} f(\vx)$ and $\matr{H} \eqdef \matr{H}_f(\vx)$.
The **quadratic model** of $f$ at $\vx$ is the function of a step $\stepvec \in \reals^p$

$$
q(\stepvec) \eqdef f(\vx) + \dprod{\vecf{g}}{\stepvec} + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\stepvec} \matr{H} \stepvec,
$$

also called the **second-order Taylor polynomial** of $f$ at $\vx$:
when the second partial derivatives of $f$ are continuous,
@thm-taylor-mv says that $f(\vx + \stepvec)$ equals the same expression
with the Hessian evaluated at a point between $\vx$ and $\vx + \stepvec$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-quadratic-model}
#### The model at $x = 2.5$

For $f(x) = \tfrac{1}{3} x^3 - 4x$ at $x = 2.5$ (@exm-newton-method),
$g = 2.5^2 - 4 = 2.25$ and $H = [2 \cdot 2.5] = [5]$, so
$q(\step) = f(2.5) + 2.25\,\step + 2.5\,\step^2$.
For $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} (x_1^2 + 3 x_2^2)$, whose Hessian is $\sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 }$ at every point,
the model at any $\vx$ equals $f(\vx + \stepvec)$ exactly (@exm-taylor-mv with $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 1/2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3/2 }$).

:::
